items.title: Ukraine races to field faster interceptors as Russia hammers its energy grid
items.originalTitle: Ukraine races to field faster interceptors as Russia hammers its energy grid
items.summary: KYIV, Ukraine — Russia is still using fast jet-powered drones to batter Ukraine’s energy facilities, bridges and other critical infrastructure at speeds beyond the reach of most of Kyiv’s drone interceptors, despite U.S. President Donald Trump’s unilateral announcement on Sunday of an energy ceasefire between the two countries. Russia began using the jets heavily in July, when their numbers jumped fivefold from the previous month.

evidenceRecords.text: KYIV, Ukraine — Russia is still using fast jet-powered drones to batter Ukraine’s energy facilities, bridges and other critical infrastructure at speeds beyond the reach of most of Kyiv’s drone interceptors, despite U.S. President Donald Trump’s unilateral announcement on Sunday of an energy ceasefire between the two countries.
Russia began using the jets heavily in July, when their numbers jumped fivefold from the previous month.

They can now reach speeds of up to 373 mph (600 km/h) — more than three times the speed of the propeller-driven Geran-2 drones they evolved from — far exceeding the top velocity of the average Ukrainian interceptor drone, air force officials told lawmakers last week.
To stop the drones, Ukraine must instead rely on F-16s, newly installed machine gun turrets that use artificial intelligence to aim and costly air-defense missiles that are in short supply globally.
“Ukraine did not strike Russian oil refining and the energy sector in general for two days after the American president announced a ceasefire in the energy sector.

But Russia did not listen to the American president,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wrote after jets seriously damaged a gas production facility in the northeastern Kharkiv region on Sunday night.
Russia launched 167 missiles and drones overnight Tuesday into Wednesday, including 77 jet-powered drones, which officials said struck one of Kyiv’s main power plants and left 600,000 without power.

Ukraine’s Air Force says they are beginning to field more effective countermeasures, but with Russia continuing to optimize the design of jet-powered drones to destroy critical infrastructure, the development of jets and anti-jet interceptors has become the latest neck-and-neck technology race on the battlefield.

Iran shipped Russia its first Shahed-131 and Shahed-136 drones in mid-August 2022, and Moscow rebranded them the Geran-1 and Geran-2 and was firing them at Ukrainian civilian infrastructure by that October.

Those propeller-driven drones were slow enough for Ukraine to build an economical defense around mobile fire teams and cheap interceptor drones rather than spending scarce missiles on every Shahed, and in February the interceptors accounted for more than 70% of Shahed downings over Kyiv .

items.title: Hegseth, service secretaries discuss ‘generational change’ of Autonomous Warfare Command
items.originalTitle: Hegseth, service secretaries discuss ‘generational change’ of Autonomous Warfare Command
items.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s vision for the planned Autonomous Warfare Command over the next two years “is that we're still iterating, we're still adapting, we're still learning, and we're moving faster and faster because we're doing it. We understand how to do it better with each iteration.” Hegseth sat down to discuss the Defense Department’s efforts to advance its autonomous capabilities with the service secretaries and the Pentagon’s top civilian for special operations during a panel Wednesday at AUSA’s annual meeting in Washington, D.C., but the discussion offered few details on what the forthcoming AUTOWARCOM, scheduled to activate by Oct. 1, 2027, will look like and how it will accomplish its mission. The secretary, who has ordered cuts to and flag officer positions across the military services, was asked why a four-star combatant command is the correct vehicle to speed up acquisition and fielding of autonomous systems. “Let's put rank where we need it to ensure we can drive change quickly,” Hegseth said. “We're going to use rank to drive change with the right people in those positions, but not just legacy formations and commands which have gathered over time and haven't led to battlefield efforts.” He did not say whether a search is on for commander candidates and what kind of experience he’s looking for. items.originalTitle: F-35C Makes First Arrested Landing Aboard A Ford Class Carrier
items.summary: A U.S. Navy F-35C has made the first arrested landing for the type aboard a Ford class aircraft carrier, with the milestone taking place aboard the future USS John F. The milestone marks a major step in testing the Navy’s stealth fighter aboard its newest carrier class, following years of challenges integrating advanced launch and recovery systems. Two F-35C test pilots assigned to Air Test and Evaluation Squadron 23 (VX-23), part of the Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD), flew to the carrier as part of an ongoing Aircraft Compatibility Testing (ACT) campaign.

evidenceRecords.text: With both solid rocket boosters fully stacked and all four RS-25 engines now installed on the Core Stage, NASA is preparing to mate the stage to the boosters and form the short stack that will roll to Launch Pad 39B for a tanking test.
The test, expected in the coming months, will also give the Artemis III crew their first full launch-day rehearsal on the pad ahead of the targeted no-earlier-than June 2027 mission.

Engineers with NASA’s Exploration Ground Systems finished stacking the twin five-segment boosters on September 30 by mating the aerodynamic nose cones to the left and right forward assemblies inside the Vehicle Assembly Building’s High Bay 3 at Kennedy Space Center.
The boosters, built by Northrop Grumman, will deliver more than 75 percent of total SLS thrust at liftoff from Pad 39B.
NASA plans to roll the short stack to Launch Pad 39B for a tanking test, during which the launch team will practice propellant loading timelines and procedures.

items.title: Ukrainian military’s access to Starlink satellite internet suddenly restricted
items.originalTitle: Ukrainian military’s access to Starlink satellite internet suddenly restricted
items.summary: Ukraine’s military has suddenly had its access to Starlink satellite internet terminals restricted as the Trump administration has increased pressure on Ukraine to halt long-range strikes on Russia’s oil industry immediately. The terminals, which are produced by Elon Musk’s SpaceX but managed by the US government, are a key component of Ukraine’s military operations and the sudden restrictions on the terminals travelling at high speeds on Tuesday evening led to the failure of several combat missions, said an adviser on military technology to Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The sudden outage came as Russia launched ballistic missiles at Ukraine without any advance warning from the US for a second night. For years, the US has provided Ukraine with intelligence when strikes were about to take place. Donald Trump has denied that his administration has cut intelligence sharing with Ukraine. Zelenskyy also indicated that the US was continuing to share intelligence with Ukraine in an interview with NPR aired on Wednesday, but confirmed that military advisers had received threats from the US that intelligence sharing could be limited. Ukraine did not receive any warning before Russia launched its first barrage of ballistic missiles on Tuesday evening, according to Col Yurii Ihnat, a spokesperson for the air force. But it did receive warnings from “foreign partners” about three subsequent barrages, leaving further confusion about whether or not the US is intentionally withholding intelligence from Ukraine.

displayTranslation.summary: 乌克兰军方对星链卫星互联网终端的访问突然受到限制，背景是特朗普政府加大了对乌克兰的压力，要求其立即停止对俄罗斯石油工业的远程打击。这些终端由埃隆·马斯克的SpaceX公司生产，但由美国政府管理，是乌克兰军事行动的关键组成部分。乌克兰总统沃洛德米尔·泽连斯基的一名军事技术顾问表示，周二晚间，对高速移动终端的突然限制导致数个作战任务失败。此次突然断网发生之际，俄罗斯连续第二晚在没有任何美方预警的情况下向乌克兰发射弹道导弹。多年来，美国一直在袭击即将发生时向乌克兰提供情报。唐纳德·特朗普否认其政府削减了与乌克兰的情报共享。泽连斯基于周三播出的NPR采访中表示，美国仍在继续与乌克兰共享情报，但证实军事顾问已收到美方威胁，称情报共享可能受到限制。乌克兰空军发言人尤里·伊格纳特上校称，周二晚间俄罗斯发动第一波弹道导弹袭击前，乌克兰未收到任何预警；但对于随后三波袭击，乌克兰收到了“外国伙伴”的预警，这使得美国是否在故意隐瞒情报更显扑朔迷离。马斯克表示，星链并未授权给使用武器的客户，乌克兰军方连接的是由美国政府运营的另一个名为“星盾”（Starshield）的网络，“这不在SpaceX的控制之下”。

items.title: SAXON Q Reports That Room-Temperature Quantum Computers Can Rival the Performance of Superconducting Processors
items.originalTitle: SAXON Q Reports That Room-Temperature Quantum Computers Can Rival the Performance of Superconducting Processors
items.summary: Insider Brief SAXON Q reported that its room-temperature diamond quantum computer achieved 77.3% success in a three-qubit Grover search, close to the cited superconducting benchmark of 78%. The system achieved 87% success when searching for two targets among eight items, with both tests exceeding the classical success limits cited in the paper. Researchers conducted the benchmark at Fraunhofer IWU in Dresden using a previous-generation system that consumes roughly 600 watts and requires no cryogenic cooling or vacuum equipment.

evidenceRecords.text: Insider Brief SAXON Q reported that its room-temperature diamond quantum computer achieved 77.3% success in a three-qubit Grover search, close to the cited superconducting benchmark of 78%.
The system achieved 87% success when searching for two targets among eight items, with both tests exceeding the classical success limits cited in the paper.
Researchers conducted the benchmark at Fraunhofer IWU in Dresden using a previous-generation system that consumes roughly 600 watts and requires no cryogenic cooling or vacuum equipment.

PRESS RELEASE — — SAXON Q , a leader in NV-center quantum computing, today released a paper showing that its room-temperature diamond-based system can perform on par with superconducting quantum computers cooled to near absolute zero.

Running Grover’s search algorithm, a standard benchmark test for quantum performance, a SAXON Q system identified a single target state 77.3% of the time using three qubits, rivaling the best published superconducting result of 78%, which required a temperature roughly 15,000 times colder.
“The assumption in quantum computing has been that you trade performance for convenience.

“Our system ran a complete quantum algorithm in an ordinary room at a customer site, and the results were similar to those of machines that require extensive infrastructure to cool them to near absolute zero.” Grover’s algorithm — also known as the “quantum search algorithm” — has been used for years to benchmark quantum computers.

It finds a marked item in an unsorted list, using fewer steps than any classical computing method can, and it is a building block for how quantum applications will approach optimization work, financial analysis, cryptography and more.
It uses a sequence that includes the qubits, single and multi-qubit gates, repeated operations and a final readout, all of which work together.

Superconducting quantum computers, by contrast, can demand upwards of 25 kilowatts and must be cooled to near absolute zero inside dilution refrigerators that require specialized facilities and chilled-water cooling.
The experiment was conducted on a previous-generation SAXON Q quantum computer, which predates its new SXQ128 and SXQ512 quantum computers announced in July.
The SXQ128 is available to order now , and SXQ512 deliveries are scheduled to begin in the second quarter of 2027.

items.title: L3Harris delivers first VAMPIRE counter-drone systems to US Army
items.originalTitle: L3Harris delivers first VAMPIRE counter-drone systems to US Army
items.summary: L3Harris Technologies has begun delivering its VAMPIRE counter-unmanned aircraft systems (C-UAS) to the US Army, with the first units arriving within two months of a USD106 million order announced in June. VAMPIRE is a self-contained weapons system designed to provide reconnaissance and precision-strike capabilities against drones and other remotely piloted aircraft. items.title: Researchers improve weather forecasts looking two to six weeks out
items.originalTitle: Researchers improve weather forecasts looking two to six weeks out
items.summary: In a new paper in Nature , the researchers describe their approach and show how it enables forecasts that for the first time beat climatologic averages between two and six weeks. “Not only does this do better on time averaged forecasts for this range, which is already very useful for farmers and members of the energy industry trying to match supply with demand, but it also improves predictions of extreme weather events, whether it’s flooding or cold spells or something else,” co-author and MIT Research Scientist Judah Cohen says.

evidenceRecords.text: In a new paper in Nature , the researchers describe their approach and show how it enables forecasts that for the first time beat climatologic averages between two and six weeks.

“Not only does this do better on time averaged forecasts for this range, which is already very useful for farmers and members of the energy industry trying to match supply with demand, but it also improves predictions of extreme weather events, whether it’s flooding or cold spells or something else,” co-author and MIT Research Scientist Judah Cohen says.

“It’s really important to predict both, but extreme events might be the most impactful part of this for society.” Joining Cohen on the paper are lead authors Hannah Guan, a Harvard College undergraduate; Soukayna Mouatadid, a University of Toronto postdoc; Genevieve Flaspohler SM ’18, PhD ’22; Paulo Orenstein, an associate professor at Brazil’s National Institute for Pure and Applied Mathematics; Jeremy Berman of the data company DTN; Jakob Schloer and Joshua Talib, researchers with the European Center for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts; and Alex Lu, Haiyu Dong, Jonathan Weyn, Zekun Ni, and

Longer forecasts In the 1970s, longtime MIT Professor Edward Lorenz came up with the idea of chaos theory to describe how tiny changes in initial weather conditions lead to completely different outcomes.

“He came up with this theoretical two-week limit where beyond that, we just can’t predict weather because the noise in the system grows so much that it overwhelms any signal you start with,” Cohen says.
